plan.summary: A cordless compact blower exhibits intermittent operation, cutting in and out unpredictably without a fixed period. The symptoms are consistent with an intermittent electrical connection, a degraded power switch/trigger contact, or motor brush wear, but the available evidence does not prove a specific point of failure.

hypotheses.mechanism: Degraded or oxidized trigger switch contacts
hypotheses.why: The tool cuts in and out and sometimes fails to start when engaged, which is commonly caused by high-resistance or intermittent mechanical contact inside the trigger switch assembly.
hypotheses.safe_test: With the battery pack removed, connect a digital multimeter in continuity or low-resistance mode across the switch terminals and cycle or gently wiggle the trigger to check for intermittent contact resistance without power.

hypotheses.mechanism: Intermittent battery interface or terminal contact
hypotheses.why: Movement or vibration during handling can cause loose terminal tabs or tarnished contacts between the tool housing and battery pack to briefly break the circuit.
hypotheses.safe_test: With the battery removed, visually inspect the tool-side receptacle terminals for spread pins, corrosion, debris, or thermal deformation without bending or shorting contacts.

hypotheses.mechanism: Worn motor brushes or intermittent commutator contact
hypotheses.why: In brushed DC motor tools, worn carbon brushes or weak brush spring tension can cause intermittent power delivery and sporadic stalling when the rotor stops on an uneven contact point.
hypotheses.safe_test: With the battery removed, manually rotate the motor fan/shaft by hand while checking resistance across the unpowered motor leads to identify dead spots or erratic contact.

plan.next_safe_check: Disconnect and remove the battery pack, then perform a visual inspection of the tool battery receptacle contacts and mechanical trigger action for loose fittings, contamination, or abnormal physical play.
plan.uncertainty: The source evidence relies on subjective creator speech and observations without electrical measurements, terminal inspections, or teardown data; motor type (brushed vs. brushless) and internal control circuitry are unverified.
